messages:
anna: Heads up — seeing spikes in auth errors and 502s in eu2. Console login failures and API token checks failing for a subset of requests.

mike: Confirmed from oncall. Alerts show controlplane-eu2 losing connections to key routing services and the autoscaler is throttling. Link to graph: https://dash.redwood/eu2/controlplane

jules: Error sample from auth-proxy: 
```
ERROR auth-proxy: grpc: connection error: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = all SubConns are TransientFailure
WARN token-verify: backend unavailable
```

leo: Newer deployments are stuck in PENDING for >6m — config-rollout jobs failing with 503 from controlplane API.

mike: Can we shift traffic? Primary plan: move non-critical hosted API traffic to us-west1 and ap-south temporarily, preserve dedicated pools in eu for customers with data locality. Any objections?

anna: Agree. Start with 30% shift for public endpoints, keep admin/console pinned to eu for now. We need a rollback path.

jules: Trying a manual scale on eu2 control plane pods but HPA is reporting `throttle: unable to acquire lock` and kube-api is flapping. Suspect control plane etcd leader election issues.

ops-engineer: Opening runbook step 2: enable failover routing policy. Running command: `redwood-route shift --from eu2 --to us-west1 --pct 30 --services public-api,embeddings`

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: route change initiated by ops-engineer at 1769987710. Observability: rerouting 30% of traffic to us-west1.

mike: Noting cost impact — us-west burst will use on-demand dedicated pools, might push estimated extra $2.5k/hr. Tagging finance for approval but we need to keep SLAs. @jules monitor GPU queue lengths.

jules: GPU queue spiking on eu2: many idle instances can't be assigned because controlplane can't allocate slots. Workaround: start emergency fallback workers in us-west staging pool. Command: `infractl start-worker --region us-west1 --type gpu-fallback --count 6`

leo: Confirmed temporary workers started. Clients rerouted and 502s dropping. Console still intermittently failing for a subset of tenants.

anna: Any sign of compromised certs or KMS? Could be auth signing failing if controlplane lost key access.

jules: KMS ok. Logs point to controlplane internal auth cache invalidation loop after failed heartbeat to router service. We're running a safe restart of controlplane-eu2 leader to force re-election.

sre-bot: sre-bot: controlplane-eu2 leader restart initiated at 1769987765 (automated from playbook). Expect 45-90s disruption to controlplane API.

mike: Noted. Keep monitoring rollout jobs. If restarts don't converge in 5m, escalate to core infra and consider region-level maintenance/evacuation.

jules: Restart completed. We're seeing controlplane API come back but with degraded performance; still seeing auth 500s for ~2% requests — investigating KV-store latency between nodes.

leo: KV-store latency metric: `etcd_election_duration_seconds` spiked to 1.2s during unrest, now trending down to 0.2s.

anna: Good. Continue gradual traffic normalization: move back 15% from us-west to eu2 when auth error rate < 0.5% for 10m.

ops-engineer: Executing: `redwood-route adjust --to eu2 --pct 15 --services public-api,embeddings`

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: route adjustment done at 1769987820.

mike: Post-mortem notes to capture: controlplane leader election sensitivity during partial network partition, autoscaler lock contention causing worker provisioning stalls, lack of graceful K8s API backpressure handling. Also include cost impact from cross-region burst.

anna: Agree. Assigning follow-ups: Jules to root-cause etcd election flakiness, Leo to autoscaler lock race, Mike to cost/finance note and traffic policy changes, Ops to update runbook with faster fallback triggers.

jules: I'll start collecting logs and timeline for the RCA. Saving snapshots: `es export --query "controlplane-eu2" --from 1769987600 --to 1769987900 --out /tmp/eu2-incident-logs.tar.gz`

mike: Thanks team. Closing incident channel when errors stable for 30m and all rollouts cleared. :thumbsup:
